clue.text: To make a short figure gain a little height is a struggle

indicators.note: a short version of the word is a truncated one, so its tail is cut away here

parts.note: the clue word supplies its own letters before trimming
HT is the standard abbreviation for height, a little bit of the word

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make a short figure look taller and finds it hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts FIGURE down to FIG; 'gain' attaches HT, the abbreviation for height; 'To make' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight is a struggle or contest between opponents.

clue.text: Pension for all the directors

parts.note: something for all is full, covering everyone
a company's directors together form its board

explanation.surface: A retirement income shared by all the company's directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pension' is the French sense of a boarding house with meals, not a retirement income.
explanation.definitionFit: At a continental pension the tariff traditionally includes lodging plus all meals, the arrangement hotels advertise by this name.

clue.text: Change tack and live a more sociable life

definitions.meaning: a sailing vessel turning onto the other tack
getting out and about, mixing with people

explanation.definitionFit: Sailors use the phrase for turning the boat onto a new tack, and it also means circulating socially, going out to visit people.

clue.text: Neat hair cut

definitions.meaning: tidy and smart in appearance
a light cut to tidy the hair

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for tidy and a noun for a light haircut at the barber's.

clue.text: Three for a tea dance

parts.note: CHA is slang for tea, from Chinese

indicators.note: three of the tea word are wanted, one written and the other two produced by repeating it

parts.note: CHA is slang for tea, from Chinese

explanation.surface: Three cups ordered for an afternoon tea dance.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is old British slang for tea; 'Three' asks for it three times over; 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American ballroom dance with a quick triple step.

clue.text: Nothing at all wrong giving one to a pastry shop

definitions.meaning: in perfect neatness, everything in its place

definitions.text: giving one to a pastry shop
definitions.meaning: a request a customer might place at a bakery for a single fruit tart

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means perfectly tidy and correct, and read literally it is a request to a bakery for a fruit tart.

clue.text: Where you expect to find brains at school

definitions.text: Where you expect to find brains
definitions.meaning: the skull, the part of the body containing the brain
the person in charge of a school, the principal

explanation.definitionFit: The skull holds the brain, and a school's principal teacher is known by the same word.

clue.text: Teacher is doubtless rattled by him

definitions.text: Teacher is doubtless rattled by him

indicators.note: rattled means shaken up, so the letters of the clue's first word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pupil caught copying would unsettle any teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rattled' shakes up the letters of TEACHER; the whole clue doubles as a description of a pupil who copies answers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil who copies in exams is the sort of person likely to disturb a teacher.

clue.text: Crime a parson headed off

indicators.note: with its head removed, the first letter of the clergyman word is dropped

explanation.surface: A vicar commits an offence, and is stopped in the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headed off' removes the P at the front of PARSON; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Going ahead with re-roofing the old church

definitions.meaning: in front, in first place
covering the roof with sheets of the metal Pb, as on old churches

explanation.definitionFit: The word means in front, and also sheets of the grey metal Pb laid on a roof, as old churches have.

clue.text: Seize your last chance to be in on a conspiracy gamble

definitions.text: Seize your last chance to be in on a conspiracy gamble

parts.words: Seize your last chance to be in on a conspiracy gamble
parts.note: a desperate final attempt, clutching at the slightest hope, like drawing lots in a plot

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as joining a plot, but it describes the drowning man's last hope; drawing lots by straws is the secondary picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a desperate attempt, clutching at any small hope of rescue like a drowning man.

clue.text: Wild parsley in the field

definitions.note: those in the field are the people taking part in a game

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the herb's letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Wild parsley growing out in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' scrambles PARSLEY; 'in the field' is shorthand for those taking part on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a team taking part in a match are out on the pitch.

clue.text: A mistake whichever way you view it

indicators.note: read forwards or backwards the word comes out the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An error that looks wrong from every angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Boob is British slang for a blunder.

clue.text: Gemstone with old copper attachment which is worn out

parts.note: jade is a green gemstone
D stood for a penny, an old copper coin, in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: A gem with an antique copper fitting that has seen better days.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the pre-1971 British penny, a copper coin; 'with' and 'attachment which is' join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaded means tired out and dulled by overuse.

clue.text: School which teaches only 10 out of the 26

definitions.text: School which teaches only 10 out of the 26

parts.words: School which teaches only 10 out of the 26
parts.note: the school's name read as letters says '...', a span covering ten of the alphabet's twenty-six letters

explanation.surface: A school with a very limited curriculum.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the school's name as E TO N: the alphabet from E through N is exactly ten of its twenty-six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous English public school near Windsor, whose name splits into a letter range.

clue.text: Assurance sought by fugitive

definitions.meaning: insurance protection, as in a policy
a hiding place someone on the run looks for

explanation.definitionFit: Insurance protection is called this, and so is the shelter a person on the run tries to take.

clue.text: Administer punishment to back parts

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the backward direction

parts.note: the clue word gives its own letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PARTS round; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone with a leather belt as a punishment.

clue.text: War artist who splashes out on his canvas

definitions.text: War artist who splashes out on his canvas

parts.words: War artist who splashes out on his canvas
parts.note: a painter of combat is the false reading; really an abstract painter flinging paint at the canvas, as Pollock did

explanation.surface: A painter of battle scenes being extravagant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'War' suggests battle, but it is fighting-as-action: the style of Jackson Pollock, dripping and splashing paint.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract expressionist who applies paint by dripping and flinging it.

clue.text: Somewhat objectionable suggestion to a drunken wine sampler

definitions.meaning: vulgar, in poor taste

definitions.text: suggestion to a drunken wine sampler
definitions.meaning: advice to sip less, split into two words

explanation.definitionFit: The word means vulgar or crass, and split in two it is advice to a tipsy sampler to sip less.

clue.text: We see toast top crumbled to serve as a vegetable dish

indicators.note: crumbled means broken into pieces, so the four words' letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone notices crumbs from the toast scattered over a side dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbled' rearranges WE SEE TOAST TOP; 'to serve as a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange-fleshed tubers served cooked as a side vegetable.

clue.text: Drive away a politician in the middle of hair treatment

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the centre of another

parts.note: shoo means drive away, as with a cat
MP is Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is chased off midway through a salon appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: A and MP go 'in the middle of' SHOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid soap used for washing the hair.

clue.text: Sailing or maybe surfing

definitions.meaning: aboard a ship
standing on a surfboard

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means aboard a ship, and literally standing on a plank such as a surfboard.

clue.text: He has a right to be told

parts.note: the clue word gives its own letters

explanation.surface: A man claims his entitlement to be informed.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn of something by report, as in 'I gather that...'.

clue.text: House dog required to leap excitedly to greet master

parts.note: a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A puppy jumps up to welcome its owner home.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring upwards in excitement, as a pet does on someone's return.

clue.text: First part of vinyl record intended only for audience to hear

definitions.meaning: the main side of a single, the one with the featured song

definitions.text: intended only for audience to hear
definitions.meaning: a stage remark the other characters supposedly do not catch

explanation.definitionFit: The main side of a single, and, unhyphenated, a stage remark spoken to the audience alone.

clue.text: Healthy and fit for work

definitions.meaning: sound in body
competent, capable

explanation.definitionFit: The word means physically sound, as in able-bodied, and capable of doing the job.

clue.text: A thread you are looking at

definitions.meaning: a ball of yarn, the old spelling clew, as Theseus used in the labyrinth
the line of text the solver is reading right now

explanation.definitionFit: The word derives from a ball of thread that guided Theseus, and it names the crossword hint in front of the solver.

clue.text: Staunch supporter

definitions.meaning: to stop a flow, as of blood
the stalk holding up a flower or leaf

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to stop a flow, and the noun is a plant's supporting stalk.

clue.text: Well liked back up in the arctic

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: polar describes the arctic regions

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round

parts.note: the clue word gives its own letters

explanation.surface: Something is back in favour up in the frozen north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns UP into PU, which goes 'in' POLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular means widely liked or admired.

clue.text: Caterer disposed to go back over the steps

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the cook's letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A caterer inclined to return the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow the same route again in reverse.

clue.text: Sort of conflict fought out on the hot-line?

definitions.text: Sort of conflict fought out on the hot-line?

parts.words: Sort of conflict fought out on the hot-line?
parts.note: a battle waged by telephone is the joke reading; really the quiet early months of WWII, 1939-40, when little fighting happened

explanation.surface: A dispute carried on by telephone between leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: The term names the period of inaction on the Western Front in 1939-40; the clue pretends it is a telephone quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical name for the period of little real fighting at the start of the Second World War.

clue.text: Modern America reveals the technical method

parts.note: US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: The United States shows off its up-to-date approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for a way of doing something, used in formal or technical contexts as in modus operandi.
